_: Kill-check for asc-09wx.10: the commit trigger handler (`handlers/session-commit.yaml`), the row that joins a session to the commits it made. The whole handler is three lines of `where` and three lines of `emit`, so the mutants are the three claims it makes and nothing else. M1 drops the `head` guard, which is the one thing that keeps a command merely MENTIONING a commit -- `npm run commit`, and any `bd create "... commit ..."` -- out of the corpus. M2 drops `is_error`, the field that keeps a commit this repository's gate refused from being counted as a commit that landed; 124 of the corpus's 4,483 rows carry it. M3 tightens the argument check to the adjacent pair `followed_by: [git, commit]`, which reads as an obvious improvement and is the one change measured to cost the most: it drops all 413 commits written `git -c user.name=... commit`. Killers were found empirically, by planting each mutant and reading the failing test names off vitest's JSON reporter, not by guessing them.

killers.test: does not match a command that only mentions the word
emits the commit a session ran, keyed on the call that ran it
carries a refused commit as the text "true", so a reader can leave it out
matches a commit whose subcommand git options come before
DOES match a git command that only mentions the word, the measured 1 in 4,483
